faqs.question: What is the HAAKE Falling Ball Viscometer C used for?
faqs.answer: It's a manual, power-free instrument for precise viscosity measurement of transparent Newtonian liquids and gases, used across chemical, pharmaceutical, food, and mineral oil industries.

faqs.question: Does this instrument need a power connection?
faqs.answer: No, it operates entirely manually, using a falling ball, calibrated tube, and stopwatch.

faqs.question: What viscosity range can it measure?
faqs.answer: 0.5 to 1,000,000 cSt, across a temperature range of -20°C to +150°C.

faqs.question: Is this instrument recognized as a reference standard?
faqs.answer: Yes, it meets DIN 53015 and ISO 12058 standards and is accepted as an official reference instrument.

faqs.question: What's included in the kit?
faqs.answer: A falling ball tube with holder, a set of six numbered balls, an instrument case, a precision thermometer, cleaning tools, a calibration sheet, and an instruction manual.

faqs.question: Does it come with a stopwatch?
faqs.answer: No, a stopwatch is required to operate the instrument but is not included.

faqs.question: What materials are the balls and tube made from?
faqs.answer: Balls 1, 2, and G, along with the falling tube, are borosilicate glass; balls 3, 4, 5, and 6 are nickel iron alloy.

faqs.question: How reproducible are the measurements?
faqs.answer: Reproducibility stays under 0.5%.

faqs.question: Does temperature control affect accuracy?
faqs.answer: Yes, accuracy is highest when paired with the precise temperature control of a circulator.

sections.description: HAAKE Falling Ball Viscometer C product information: measurement principle, standards compliance, and included components.

body.text: Measuring accuracy ranks among the highest available in any type of viscometer, particularly when paired with the precise temperature control of a circulator.
The instrument measures the viscosity of transparent Newtonian liquids and gases directly, using the falling ball principle rather than powered rotational or electronic sensing.
It meets the requirements of German DIN 53015 and ISO 12058 standards, and is accepted as an official reference instrument, used to validate other viscometers rather than needing validation itself.
Viscosity range covers 0.5 to 1,000,000 cSt, across a temperature range of -20°C to +150°C.
Reproducibility stays under 0.5%, a tight tolerance for a fully manual instrument.
The falling tube and balls 1, 2, and G are borosilicate glass; balls 3, 4, 5, and 6 are nickel iron alloy, giving a range of ball densities to match different sample viscosities.
A stopwatch is required to operate the instrument; it is not included.
Applications span the chemical industry (polymer solutions, solvents), pharmaceutical industry (raw materials, glycerine), food industry (sugar solutions), and mineral oil industry (oils).

body: Some measurements gain credibility precisely because they don't depend on electronics that could drift, fail, or need recalibration against a hidden internal standard. Falling Ball Viscometer C is one of those instruments.

Compliance with DIN 53015 and ISO 12058 isn't a marketing claim, it means the instrument is accepted as an official reference, the kind other viscometers get checked against rather than the other way around.
Reproducibility under 0.5% holds that reference-grade standard even with no power connection involved, particularly when the sample's temperature is controlled precisely with a circulator.

body.text: HAAKE Viscotester 3 works either handheld or mounted on a lab stand, giving flexibility to measure wherever the process actually is, not just at a fixed bench location.
Viscosity range covers 30 to 400,000 mPas on catalog number 399-0112, or 1.5 to 1,300 mPas on catalog number 399-0111, matching the instrument to the sample type.
Smart alignment is built directly into the design and visualized through an electronic level, removing guesswork from correct instrument positioning.
Quick coupling of measuring geometries makes swapping rotors fast, and color coding on each geometry, paired with a range indicator, ensures the correct rotor gets selected every time.
An adaptable display brightness keeps readings visible in any lighting environment, from a bright production floor to a dim storage area.
The instrument remembers the reference point measurement automatically, so comparing a current reading against that baseline takes no extra setup.
It runs on battery or power supply, and the entire kit, base unit, holder, measuring cup, rotors, batteries, and adapter, ships in a ready-to-go carrying case.
HAAKE Viscotester 3 replaces the discontinued HAAKE Viscotester 1 Plus and 2 Plus, with results compatible for labs upgrading from a Viscotester 2 Plus.
